response: Ongoing clinical studies, specifically randomized controlled trials (RCTs), may not have enough power to definitively settle the issue of whether the length of storage of transfused red blood cells has a negative impact on clinical outcomes. However, as a precautionary measure, reducing the maximum storage time to 35 days is advisable. This suggests that while clinical studies are being conducted to investigate this connection, a conservative approach to the storage time of transfused red blood cells is recommended to potentially minimize any adverse effects on clinical outcomes.
